sections.h2: Where is Marshalltown, Iowa, and how did it get its name?
sections.html:
Marshalltown is the county seat of Marshall County, in central Iowa, at about 899 feet of elevation. The city covers roughly 19.2 square miles, and Hardin, Grundy, Tama, Jasper and Story counties border the county around it.

Henry Anson was the first European settler. He arrived in April 1851 and built a log cabin on high ground between the Iowa River and Linn Creek, and a plaque at 112 West Main Street marks the spot. Anson named the town Marshall in 1853 after Marshall, Michigan. It became Marshalltown in 1862 because another Marshall already existed in Henry County.

The county seat moved here from Marietta in 1863, and the route of an east-west railroad decided the question. The Cedar Rapids and Missouri River Railroad had reached town in 1862, and the line later passed to the Chicago and North Western and then Union Pacific.

sections.h2: What are the main Marshalltown housing and population figures?
sections.html:
Marshalltown had 27,591 residents in the 2020 census, and the Census Bureau estimates 27,536 as of July 1, 2025. The census counts were 26,009 in 2000, 27,552 in 2010 and 27,591 in 2020, so the city has changed slowly in size.

With a median home value of $127,700, a repair bill of even $20,000 is a meaningful share of what a house is worth. Many owners of older houses run that math before they decide between repairing and selling as-is.

sections.h2: Who are the biggest employers in Marshalltown?
sections.html:
The largest employer is JBS pork processing, with 2,700 jobs, and the city's 2024 financial report lists 14 employers that together account for 8,506 jobs. Manufacturing, health care, education and retail make up most of the list.

Plant employment shapes the housing market. When a large employer changes shifts or headcount, buyers and renters shift with it. Federal agents raided the Swift plant, now JBS, in 1996 and again in 2006, and one study estimated the 2006 raid caused a recession lasting six months to a year.

sections.h2: Who lives in Marshalltown, and how has that changed?
sections.html:
Hispanic or Latino residents made up 31.29 percent of Marshalltown in 2020, up from 12.55 percent in 2000. The growth came mainly from immigrants from Mexico in the 1990s and 2000s, followed by a smaller group of Burmese refugees in the 2010s.

The median age was 36.7 in 2020, and the 2023 American Community Survey put median household income at $68,854 and the poverty rate at 14.0 percent. Households average 2.62 people, so a three-bedroom family house is the type of property many local buyers are likely to be shopping for.

sections.h2: What did the 2018 tornado and 2020 derecho do to Marshalltown houses?
sections.html:
An EF3 tornado crossed downtown Marshalltown on July 19, 2018, with peak winds of 145 mph. It stayed on the ground for 23 minutes along an 8.41 mile path up to 1,200 yards wide, destroyed the courthouse spire and injured 23 people, with no deaths.

Two months later, city officials said more than 1,800 homes were affected and 60 carried condemnation placards. FEMA estimated more than 2,000 buildings were damaged, and at that time it had denied individual assistance to homeowners and renters. An earlier F3 tornado hit the south side on April 23, 1961.

A derecho on August 10, 2020, with reported winds near 99 mph, brought a second round of damage. A week later nearly 7,000 residents still had no power, and city parks lost many trees.

  • Ask whether past storm repairs were permitted and finished
  • Keep roof and insurance records, since buyers and appraisers ask for them
  • Expect inspectors to look hard at roofs, chimneys and trees near the house
  • An unrepaired, storm-damaged house can still be sold as-is for cash

sections.h2: What are Marshalltown's rental registration and inspection rules?
sections.html:
Marshalltown requires every rental unit to be registered, and new rental units must pass inspection before anyone moves in. Existing rentals pay $25 per unit for annual registration, with a $25 late fee per parcel plus finance charges.

The city lists application fees of $75 for new or newly rented units that are empty, and $500 for previously occupied units that were never registered. A change of ownership for an already registered property is exempt. Rental units are generally inspected about every three years.

  • First unit inspected: $90
  • Second unit: $50
  • Third through fifteenth units: $20 each
  • Complexes of 16 or more units: capped at $400

If you are selling a rented house, a buyer who plans to keep it as a rental should ask whether the unit is registered and when it was last inspected. A $500 unregistered-unit fee is the type of cost that can surprise a new owner. The Rental Housing Division is at 641-754-6582.

sections.h2: How does Marshalltown handle nuisance and code complaints?
sections.html:
The city's Code Enforcement Office handles nuisance abatement, property maintenance and zoning violations, with examples including tall grass, junk vehicles and garbage. Complaints can be made by phone, through the city's online form, or in person at 36 N. Center Street.

A property owner who receives a Code Violation Notice can use the city's appeal request form. The city's page does not give deadlines, so read any notice closely and call the office, 641-754-5759, if the dates are unclear. A cash buyer can purchase a house with an open violation as-is, so the cleanup does not have to be finished before closing.

sections.h2: What schools, roads and transit serve Marshalltown?
sections.html:
The Marshalltown Community School District serves the city, with Marshalltown High School, six elementary schools, one intermediate school and a middle school for grades 7 and 8. The East Marshall district covers small parts of the city limits, and Marshalltown Community College sits in town.

U.S. Route 30 bypasses the city to the south, Iowa Highway 14 runs through the center and Iowa Highway 330 is an expressway to Des Moines. Marshalltown Municipal Transit runs local buses, Trailways provides intercity service, and the nearest commercial airport is Des Moines International, 53 miles southwest.

Winters are cold: the average January high is 27.5 degrees, the July high is 83.5, and annual snowfall averages 25.3 inches. Records run from 112 degrees to minus 35.

sections.h2: How do Marshall County taxes and the Iowa transfer tax work for a seller?
sections.html:
Marshall County taxes are due in two halves, September 1 and March 1, and become delinquent on October 1 and April 1. The Treasurer's office is in the courthouse at 1 E. Main Street, Suite 130, and can be reached at 641-754-6360.

Owners with unpaid taxes get notices on November 1 and May 1. The publication fee is added May 1, and delinquent parcels are advertised from June 1 ahead of the annual tax sale. A buyer who redeems a parcel after the sale pays 2 percent interest per month with guaranteed funds.

For the deed, Iowa Code 428A.1 sets the transfer tax at 80 cents per $500 of value above the first $500, and a declaration of value goes to the recorder with the deed. On the median value of $127,700, the illustration is $127,200 divided by $500, rounded up to 255, times $0.80, or $204.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Marshalltown house work?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the mortgage step, so closing depends on the title work and your schedule instead of a lender's timeline. You send us the address and condition, we review it, and if you want to proceed, a title company handles the deed and payoffs.

This fits situations common in Marshalltown: a rental with deferred inspection items, a house with leftover storm damage, or an inherited property that nobody wants to renovate.

faqs.q: How many homes did the 2018 Marshalltown tornado affect?
faqs.a: Two months after the tornado, city officials said more than 1,800 homes were affected and 60 had condemnation placards. FEMA estimated that more than 2,000 buildings were damaged.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Marshalltown?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 estimate for owner-occupied homes in Marshalltown is $127,700. The median gross rent is $891.

faqs.q: Do Marshalltown landlords have to register rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. New rental units must be registered and inspected before occupancy, and existing units pay $25 per unit each year. Rentals are generally inspected about every three years.

faqs.q: When are Marshall County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. They become delinquent on October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marshalltown house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can buy a house as-is, including one with open nuisance or maintenance notices. Read the notice and talk to the Code Enforcement Office about deadlines before you sign anything.

faqs.q: Who is the largest employer in Marshalltown?
faqs.a: JBS pork processing, with 2,700 jobs in the city's 2024 financial report. Emerson / Fisher Controls is next at 1,100.
